follow-up time: Until hospital discharge for mothers and long-term for newborns
exposure: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
Timing of delivery (before or after ECMO cannulation)
outcome: Maternal and fetal short- and long-term outcomes
cohort: 24 critically ill pregnant women with severe ARDS supported by ECMO: 11 cannulated during pregnancy and 13 cannulated after emergency delivery
finding: Continuing pregnancy on ECMO support carries a significant risk of fetal death but improves prematurity-related morbidity in surviving newborns, with no difference in maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: Fetal survival was higher when ECMO was initiated after delivery (92% vs. 55%), suggesting potential benefits of delaying delivery in mothers with severe ARDS requiring ECMO.
gest_age: Median 25 weeks (range 21-29) for those cannulated during pregnancy; 32 weeks (range 17-39) for those with delivery before ECMO
